statement: Files with the same name in the folder typed into the dialog are deleted and replaced, for any user. Only administrators also have ownership of that folder, and of an existing language subfolder, taken over and full control granted. The folder defaults to the Windows policy folder.

evidence.shows: Destination text defaults to the Windows policy folder
Same-named files deleted then moved, with no administrator check
Administrator only: access rules reset, ownership of existing folder taken
Administrator only: privileges enabled and destination ownership taken

statement: The package is fetched over HTTPS from one fixed Microsoft address and unpacked, with no signature or hash check by this code. A compromised or substituted package on that host, or a compromised trust store or proxy, would put altered definitions into the chosen destination, the Windows policy folder by default.

evidence.shows: Fixed HTTPS download address
Downloaded and unpacked with no integrity check
Only top-level definition files, current-culture and en-US folders are moved
Destination only defaults to the Windows policy folder

statement: The application permits the older TLS 1.0 and 1.1 protocol versions beside 1.2, for every web request it makes; the package download is the only one found. A comment gives Vista compatibility as the reason. The code does not show an older version being used.

evidence.shows: Tls, Tls11 and Tls12 enabled process-wide, comment cites Vista compatibility
Package download is the web call affected

statement: The data is a Microsoft installer package, defined by Microsoft. It is saved to a scratch file and unpacked to a folder tree. Only the definition files at the top, the language folder matching the current culture and the en-US fallback are moved; other languages are discarded.

evidence.shows: Package saved to scratch file
Unpack folder
Top-level files, current-culture folder and en-US moved
Whole scratch folder deleted, leaving other languages out

statement: The download and unpack have no timeout or cancel. While they run the dialog refuses to close and its buttons are disabled, so a stalled connection or hung installer program leaves the dialog, and its modal owner window, unusable until the process is killed.

evidence.shows: Closing is cancelled while busy
Close, Start and Browse disabled while busy
Download call blocks with no timeout
Unpack waits for exit indefinitely

statement: The move deletes each same-named destination file before moving its replacement, and the sequence is not atomic. A failure part-way, such as a disk or permission error or a changed package layout, can leave the destination, by default the system policy folder, with a mix of old and new files and ownership already changed.

evidence.shows: Fixed inner folder name inside the package
Old file deleted before new one moved
Ownership changed first, then several separate moves, including a required en-US folder
On failure only a generic message; nothing rolled back

statement: The installer program is started by bare name, so the system's search order, not the code, decides which executable runs. The scratch and unpack folders are fixed names, not emptied before use, so leftovers of an earlier failed run, which is never cleaned up, sit in the next unpack target.

evidence.shows: Started as msiexec with no path
Fixed scratch folder, created but not emptied
Fixed unpack folder under scratch
Cleanup only on the success path
